RagShortTexts: Transport between watersheds needs an overland link.
Workers, animals, tracks and permission affect transfer.

Variants.Content: Watershed links require hauling, carrying or changing vessels. Water cargo becomes a land load, with tracks, seasons and permissions affecting labor. Dragging the whole boat may cost more than unloading; receivers and lodging must be found beyond.
Portage escorts divide between boats and goods and keep the receiving party in contact. Heavy loads demand protection around handover points, not one river alone.
Portage income needs maintained tracks, workers and recognized passage. Unexpected demands divert traders; a charge should provide an actual onward connection.
Porters and animals need food, rest and maintained gear. Payment tied only to final sale leaves workers carrying the cost of muddy tracks or delayed boats.
